2020_144_012120org_reg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education held its combined Organizational and Regular Meeting on January 21, 2020 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, covering annual officer elections, the reappointment of Rick West as Treasurer for January through December 2020, designation of eleven depository institutions and five law firms, and the consent-agenda Treasurer's Report for November 2019. That report records total check disbursements of $10,154,749.94 and total disbursements in the period of $12,543,940.19. Unaudited General Fund statements for July 1 through November 30, 2019 show actual revenues of $41,171,251 against actual expenditures of $46,561,861.

**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education Organizational and Regular Meeting, Tuesday, January 21, 2020, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Superintendent Richard M. Machesky's agenda memo sets the order: acting chairperson, temporary secretary Judy Holmes, then election of president, vice president and secretary, each serving until December 31, 2020, with four votes required.

**Organizational actions**
- Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, appointed Treasurer for the period January through December 2020 as a nonvoting officer.
- Fund depository and investment resolution naming Bank of America, Charter One Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Huntington Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. and PNC Bank; investments per Board Policy 5000.06 and Section 380.1223(1)(h) of the Revised School Code.
- Legal counsel for calendar 2020: Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Lusk Albertson; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; Beier Howlett, P.C.
- Superintendent designated Deputy Secretary; Judy Holmes designated to post meeting notices; 2020 meeting calendar adopted (regular meetings February 25 through December 15, 2020, plus January 19, 2021; workshops at 6:00 p.m. including a Saturday, March 7, 2020 Winter Retreat).

**Recognitions**
Adam Burns of Athens High School and Athens TV students for the Michigan Arctic Grayling Initiative; Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, for the 2020 National Excellence in Literacy Leadership Award; and retiring board member Paula Fleming for more than 19 years of service, with proclamations read by Mayor Ethan Baker and State Representative Padma Kuppa.

**Business and other items**
Bid Pack #26 Re-Bid for the Athens High School pool awarded to Contrast Mechanical (scaffolding, $78,000.00) and Southeastern Tile ($109,518.00), total contract awards $187,518.00 plus 8% contingency $15,001.44 for $202,519.44, funded from the 2016 and 2019 Capital Projects Funds and the Sinking Fund. Operations vehicle purchase awarded to Gorno Ford for $143,339.00 under MiDEAL State Contract #071B1300005 from the 2019-2020 General Fund. Four probationary teaching contracts recommended (Alexia Mancilla-Jackson, Jennifer Kuntz, Laura Stedman, Claire Reid). Board President Karl Schmidt's attendance at the National Equity Project "Leading for Equity" institute in Itasca, Illinois, February 26-29, 2020 ($1,800) requires resolution approval under Board Policy 1000.01. 2020 board committee assignments adopted.

**Identification.** Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education agenda packet for the Organizational and Regular Meeting of Tuesday, January 21, 2020, 7:00 p.m., at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Superintendent Richard M. Machesky, Ed.D., supplied the agenda memo.

**Organizational business.** The prior year's president opens; Judy Holmes is appointed temporary secretary; president, vice president and secretary are elected to serve until December 31, 2020, with four votes required, roll call rotating among Philippart, Schmidt, Wilson, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hauff and Hammond. Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, is appointed Treasurer for January through December 2020 as a nonvoting officer.

The fund depository and investment resolution designates Bank of America, Charter One Bank, JP Morgan Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Huntington Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF (Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Plus, managed by PFM Asset Management, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank), Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank. Checks carry Rick West's facsimile signature; in emergencies West or Superintendent Machesky may hand-sign on the Bank of America General Fund and Payroll accounts. PNC Bank accounts pay Troy Career Center expenses; a Comerica Bank account pays flexible spending claims by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc. Investments follow Board Policy 5000.06, and the Treasurer may combine money from more than one fund under subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. Legal counsel for calendar 2020: Clark Hill, PLC; Collins & Blaha, P.C.; Lusk Albertson; Thrun Law Firm, P.C.; and Beier Howlett, P.C. The Superintendent continues as Deputy Secretary and Judy Holmes as the person posting meeting notices. Regular meetings are set for February 25, March 17, April 21, May 19, June 2 (at Athens), June 16, July 21, August 18, September 15, October 20, November 17 and December 15, 2020, and January 19, 2021, with a Saturday, March 7, 2020 Winter Retreat among the 6:00 p.m. workshops.

**Recognitions.** Adam Burns, Technology Education/English teacher at Athens High School, and Athens TV students Ellen Bedford, Abby Bright, Grace Bright, Grace Joo and Madison Strachan are recognized for the Michigan Arctic Grayling Initiative; Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, for the 2020 National Excellence in Literacy Leadership Award from Reading Recovery Teacher Leaders; and Paula Fleming, retiring after more than 19 years and moving to Arkansas, with proclamations from Mayor Ethan Baker and State Representative Padma Kuppa.

**Consent agenda minutes.** Items A-G cover the corrected November 12, 2019 workshop (David Hulings, motivational leadership coach), the December 3, 2019 workshop (Philippart absent; Paul Wills of Plante Moran; Plante Moran CRESA enrollment update), the December 17, 2019 special meeting (Fleming and Gottlieb absent; Section 1 to be rebid with an RFP after the first of the year; Resolution 19-095 closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, PA 267, Section 8(c), with Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt and Wilson voting yes), the closed session, the December 17 regular meeting and a special workshop. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

At the December 17, 2019 regular meeting, Resolution 19-096 approved the consent agenda 5-0; Resolution 19-097 approved personnel (New Hire - Murray); Resolution 19-098 awarded Bond/BSSF Bid Pack 26 from the 2016 and 2019 Capital Projects Funds and the Sinking Fund - R & E Development $698,155.00; Hewett Company exterior doors/windows for the AHS Pool $1,036,050.00; Seven Brothers Painting $50,743.00; MCMI $337,700.00; Great Lakes Power & Lighting $789,000.00; Contrast Mechanical $1,111,000.00; Air Solutions $23,500.00; total contract awards $4,046,148.00, contingency $323,691.84, total $4,369,839.84. Resolution 19-099 adopted a Reimbursement Resolution for School Building and Site Bonds reciting the September 17, 2019 authorization of bonds not to exceed $6,100,000 for acquisition of real property and a building and its renovation, equipping and furnishing, under Treas. Reg. sections 1.150-2, 1.150-1(b), 1.150-2(c), 1.150-2(h) and 1.148-1, with reimbursement allocation not later than 18 months after the expenditure or placed-in-service date and no more than three years. Student representatives Pranay Gupta, Noah Germilhac, Amanda Kovacs and Noah Scudder reported.
